claim: The novel-NME backbone this model tracks accounts for roughly 49 to 57 percent of the shared resource load actually observed, so the remainder is carried as fixed exogenous background demand rather than being ignored.

claim: The overlap coefficient rho = 0.60 used to combine the four probability-of-success levers is set so the model reproduces Agent C's stated joint band rather than being chosen freely.

figures.metric: overlap coefficient rho
figures.denominator_def: coefficient in q_joint = q_max + (1 - rho) x sum(other q)

derivation: Agent C states that improving B1, B2, B8 and B10 each by 10 percent yields at most 11-26 percent, not the 21 percent naive sum [E-3097]. With q = f x theta / 10 per lever (0.0135, 0.0050, 0.0075, 0.0015) the model's budget-free naive sum is +20.75 percent, reproducing C's 21 percent. rho = 0.60 gives q_joint = 0.0135 + 0.4 x 0.0140 = 0.0191 and a joint effect of +14.42 percent, inside C's 11-26 percent band. rho is therefore calibrated to one published band, not measured; it is an assumption with a stated target.

Risk-adjusted 1,318.9 against DiMasi's 1,395 [E-1002] is -5.5 percent; capitalized 2,790.7 against DiMasi's 2,558 [E-1001] is +9.1 percent, and against his 2,870 including post-approval R&D [E-1002] is -2.8 percent. claim: Cutting discovery duration by 80 percent with probability of success held constant produces exactly zero change in annual approvals in the model, and a 5.7 percent reduction in capitalized cost per approval.

figures.metric: change in annual approvals under scenario S1
figures.denominator_def: novel drug approvals per year relative to the S0 baseline

derivation: Scenario S1. Approvals 50.00 -> 50.00 (+0.00 percent). Mean cycle time 13.50 -> 9.90 years (-26.7 percent). Capitalized cost 2,790.7 -> 2,631.4 USD million (-5.7 percent). Risk-adjusted and out-of-pocket cost are unchanged to the decimal, because neither depends on duration. The result is structural, not parametric: with probability of success unchanged, the only channel through which duration can raise steady-state output is by freeing a scarce resource, and discovery duration occupies none of the sixteen modelled resources.

claim: Raising Phase II probability of success by 50 percent, with no change to any timeline, raises modelled annual approvals by 31.8 percent and cuts risk-adjusted cost per approval by 24.4 percent - the largest single-lever gain of any mandated scenario.

Mean cycle time RISES from 13.50 to 15.03 years, because more survivors load the Phase III patient resource (utilisation 0.83 -> 0.96) and lengthen its queue. Under a fixed R&D budget the mechanism is exact: approvals = budget / risk-adjusted cost per approval, so 1,318.9/996.9 = 1.323, against the modelled 1.318 once the phase III queue is netted off.

claim: Multiplying candidate inflow fivefold with every capacity including the R&D budget held at current levels changes annual approvals by exactly zero, because the budget rations the additional candidates out at the point of entry.

figures.denominator_def: novel drug approvals per year relative to the S0 baseline

derivation: Scenario S6. Capital utilisation is 1.00 at baseline, so a fivefold rise in candidates is throttled to a factor of 1.00 at the discovery gate and every downstream utilisation returns to its baseline value. This is not a modelling artefact to be smoothed away: it is the arithmetic statement that a fivefold pipeline needs a fivefold budget, and the observed direction of travel in early-stage capital is contraction, not expansion [E-3057][E-3058]. Scenario S6b removes the budget identity in order to expose the physical ordering underneath it.

Binding: nhp_tox 1.00, then gmp_lentiviral 1.00 and gmp_plasmid. Mean cycle time 13.50 -> 18.45 years and capitalized cost 2,791 -> 4,106 USD million, both driven purely by queueing. claim: Setting discovery duration to zero removes 33.3 percent of elapsed development time and 7.0 percent of capitalized cost per approval, and changes annual approvals by exactly zero; making discovery both instantaneous and free removes 41.0 percent of capitalized cost, 28.1 percent of risk-adjusted cost and 5.1 percent of true out-of-pocket cost, still with zero change in annual approvals.

figures.denominator_def: capitalized cost per approved novel drug, modality-weighted, 11 percent cost of capital

derivation: Amdahl envelope. Time: discovery is 4.5 of 13.5 years, 4.5/13.5 = 33.3 percent, and the model returns 13.50 -> 9.00 years exactly. Capitalized, duration only: 2,790.7 -> 2,595.7 = -7.0 percent (the discovery spend is still incurred, only its compounding horizon shortens). Capitalized, duration and cost both zero: 2,790.7 -> 1,647.6 = -41.0 percent. Risk-adjusted: 1,318.9 -> 948.2 = -28.1 percent. True out-of-pocket for one successful programme: 263.5 -> 250.0 = -5.1 percent, because discovery is only 13.5 of 263.5 USD million of the cash spent on a molecule that works. Annual approvals: 50.00 -> 50.00, +0.00 percent. Agent A's independent arithmetic gave 21-41 percent of time and 40-43 percent of capitalized cost [E-1094]; Agent C gave 23-37 percent of time [E-3098]. All three agree.

claim: Under a fivefold candidate inflow with physical capacity frozen, the modelled output gain is distributed unevenly across modalities: small molecules and peptides rise 1.87-fold while antibodies and ADCs fall to 0.50 of their baseline output, because rationing of a scarce shared input reallocates it toward the modalities that consume least of it.

figures.denominator_def: modality approvals per year in scenario S6b divided by the same modality in S0

derivation: Scenario S6b modality table: small_molecule 22.54 -> 42.10 (1.87x), antibody_mab 15.02 -> 7.55 (0.50x), protein 4.37 -> 3.05 (0.70x), peptide 2.88 -> 5.38 (1.87x), vaccine 1.78 -> 2.40 (1.35x), adc 1.16 -> 0.58 (0.50x), rna_antisense 0.49 -> 0.56 (1.14x), gene_therapy 0.56 -> 0.33 (0.59x), rna_sirna 0.55 -> 0.63 (1.14x), cell_therapy_carT 0.65 -> 0.83 (1.28x). Mechanism: rationing is applied multiplicatively in proportion to each modality's intensity of use of the scarce resource, so antibodies and ADCs (non-human-primate weight 1.4 against a 0.93 mean, plus aseptic fill-finish) are clipped hardest and autologous cell therapy (NHP weight 0.2) least. The direction of this result depends on the intensity weights, which are relative judgements rather than measured animal counts, so the magnitudes should be read as an ordering rather than a forecast.
